title: Replicating Activation-Based Detection Using Only the Shallowest 10% of Layers

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: knowing the earliest layer with high AUROC determines minimum cost for real-time safety filters. Cross-model comparison reveals generalizability of cheap detectors.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Training linear probes at multiple layers across 2 models is intermediate. Requires activation extraction at specific layers and standard probe training. Manageable with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused: train probes at 7 layer depths for 2 models, plot AUROC vs. depth. Clear deliverable with bounded scope.

novelty.reasoning: The Alert paper (2026) directly studies early-layer jailbreak detection with shallow-layer activations. Anthropic's cost-effective classifiers work demonstrates minimal-compute detection using representation re-use. The specific question of 'shallowest 10% of layers' is partially addressed by these works, though a systematic cross-model AUROC-vs-depth curve is a useful contribution. The core finding that shallow layers carry jailbreak signal is established.

evidence.source: Alert: Zero-shot LLM Jailbreak Detection via Internal Discrepancy (arXiv 2601.03600, 2026)
evidence.finding: Performs early detection within shallow layers of the LLM, requiring only a single forward propagation and a lightweight classifier, directly studying layer-depth vs. detection performance.

evidence.source: Cost-Effective Constitutional Classifiers via Representation Re-use (Anthropic, 2025)
evidence.finding: Studies representation-based safety classifiers with minimal computational overhead, showing a linear probe at each token performs similar to a model with 2% of parameters.
